Buying a used aviation headset: 10 checks before gifting it

A used aviation headset can look like a bargain while leaving important questions unanswered. Before making it a gift, establish the exact model, condition, service options, and return terms. This checklist helps organize due diligence; it is not a technical inspection or a claim that any used listing is suitable.

By Pilot Gift Guide · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Involve the pilot before purchase and consider a reputable seller with clear documentation. Ask the manufacturer about support for the particular model. If condition cannot be assessed adequately, choose a contribution toward equipment instead of turning the gift into an uncertain repair project.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    Exact model and version

    Ask for identifying photographs and a complete model name. Similar housings can conceal different connectors, features, and production versions.

  2. 2

    Seller’s ownership information

    Request reasonable evidence of where the headset came from. Be cautious when the listing cannot explain missing accessories or inconsistent identifying details.

  3. 3

    Connector and power configuration

    Confirm these with the recipient and manufacturer information. A lower price is not useful if the configuration does not fit the intended aircraft.

  4. 4

    Cable condition

    Request clear images and a candid condition report. Visible damage or an uncertain repair history deserves professional assessment rather than optimistic assumptions.

  5. 5

    Ear cushions and head pad

    Check wear and replacement-part availability. Include any necessary refresh in the total budget rather than comparing only the advertised price.

  6. 6

    Microphone condition

    Ask about damage and service history. The pilot should arrange an appropriate functional assessment instead of relying on a photo alone.

  7. 7

    Manufacturer support

    Confirm whether service and parts are available for that exact model. Do not assume a familiar brand still supports every older headset.

  8. 8

    Warranty transfer terms

    Ask the manufacturer or authorized seller what applies. Remaining age on a product does not automatically establish transferable warranty coverage.

  9. 9

    Return and inspection window

    Read the actual written terms and who pays return shipping. An expensive gift needs time for the recipient to assess it properly.

  10. 10

    Complete delivered cost

    Add shipping, taxes, approved replacement parts, and any known service work. Compare that total with current alternatives before deciding it is a bargain.
